html:
A Punjabi Sufi poet who lived from about 1680 to 1757, mostly at Kasur near Lahore. He is one of the greatest poets of the Punjabi language.

He came from a family of Sayyids, said to descend from the Prophet, and shocked them by taking as his spiritual guide Shah Inayat, a Qadiri Sufi from a lowly gardener caste. Much of his poetry is about longing for this teacher and for God, often in the voice of a woman waiting for her beloved.

He wrote mainly kafis, short sung lyrics. They mock religious hypocrisy and the walls between Muslim, Hindu and Sikh, and say that God is found within, not in mosque, temple or learned books. He wrote in the Punjab of the late Mughal years, a time of war and disorder, and in the same spirit as Guru Nanak and Kabir before him.

His songs belong to Sufi tradition but are loved across religions, in Pakistan and India alike. They are sung as qawwali, folk song and modern pop, including on Coke Studio.
sum: A Punjabi Sufi poet who lived from about 1680 to 1757, mostly at Kasur near Lahore. He is one of the greatest poets of the Punjabi language.
